# core/x25519.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/x25519.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

X25519, the Diffie-Hellman function on Curve25519 (RFC
7748), with field elements of 16 limbs of 16 bits in the style of TweetNaCl.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and a result is
32 bytes. Not proved: that the result is RFC 7748's (the tests check its
vectors, including the iterated ones, and a Diffie-Hellman agreement), or
that the code is constant time (the ladder swaps with a mask, and no branch
or index depends on the scalar, but nothing checks that).

A field element is a `Vec[u64]` of 16 limbs; after `fe_carry` each limb is
below 2^16 + 38. The sums of limbs are wrapped (`wrap_add`, `wrap_mul`) on
purpose: they stay far below 2^64 for such limbs, so the tests rather than
a proof show the field arithmetic right.

`import "core/x25519.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`x25519`](#x25519) | X25519. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `x25519`

```bastio
fn x25519(k: &Bytes, u: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(k) == 32 && blen(u) == 32
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

X25519: the scalar `k` (32 bytes, clamped as RFC 7748 says) times the
point whose u-coordinate is `u` (32 bytes): 32 bytes. With `u` the base
point (the byte 9, then zeros) it gives a public key.

Example:

```bastio
let mut k = balloc(32);
let mut u = balloc(32);
let mut i = 0;
while i < 32
  invariant i <= 32 && blen(k) == 32 && blen(u) == 32
{
  bset(&mut k, i, 7);
  i = i + 1;
}
bset(&mut u, 0, 9);
let pub = x25519(k, u);
let n = blen(pub);
bfree(pub);
bfree(u);
bfree(k);
if n != 32 { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `fe_zero`

```bastio
fn fe_zero() -> Vec[u64]
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: a field element equal to 0.

### `fe_copy`

```bastio
fn fe_copy(a: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: a copy of `a`.

### `fe_carry`

```bastio
fn fe_carry(o: &mut Vec[u64])
  requires vlen(o) == 16
  ensures vlen(o) == 16
```

Internal: moves the carries of `o` up, and the carry out of the top limb
back into the bottom one times 38 (2^256 is 38 modulo 2^255 - 19).

### `fe_add`

```bastio
fn fe_add(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a + b`.

### `fe_sub`

```bastio
fn fe_sub(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a - b`, computed as `a + 4p - b` so that no limb goes negative.

### `fe_mul`

```bastio
fn fe_mul(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16 && vlen(b) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a * b`.

### `fe_mul_small`

```bastio
fn fe_mul_small(a: &Vec[u64], k: u64) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a` times the small constant `k`.

### `fe_inv`

```bastio
fn fe_inv(a: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 16
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: `a` to the power p - 2, the inverse of `a` (0 for 0).

### `fe_cswap`

```bastio
fn fe_cswap(p: &mut Vec[u64], q: &mut Vec[u64], bit: u64)
  requires vlen(p) == 16 && vlen(q) == 16 && bit <= 1
  ensures vlen(p) == 16 && vlen(q) == 16
```

Internal: swaps `p` and `q` if `bit` is 1, and leaves them if it is 0.

### `fe_unpack`

```bastio
fn fe_unpack(b: &Bytes) -> Vec[u64]
  requires blen(b) == 32
  ensures vlen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the field element of the 32 little-endian bytes of `b` (the top
bit is ignored).

### `fe_reduce_once`

```bastio
fn fe_reduce_once(o: &mut Vec[u64])
  requires vlen(o) == 16
  ensures vlen(o) == 16
```

Internal: one step of the final reduction. Adds 19; if that reaches 2^255
the value was at least p, and the sum without the bit 255 (the value minus
p) replaces it. Chosen by a mask, not a branch.

### `fe_pack`

```bastio
fn fe_pack(a: &Vec[u64]) -> Bytes
  requires vlen(a) == 16
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

Internal: the 32 little-endian bytes of `a` reduced modulo 2^255 - 19.

### `x25519_bit`

```bastio
fn x25519_bit(k: &Bytes, t: u64) -> u64
  requires blen(k) == 32 && t < 256
  ensures result <= 1
```

Internal: the bit `t` of the scalar `k`.
